clue.text: Nice crop developed by American astronomer

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters before it are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A fine harvest is credited to a scientist from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomer is Polish, not American: 'American' only supplies the closing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolaus Copernicus was the Renaissance scientist who put the sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Cod, for example — better choice ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so just the final letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
last letter of choice

explanation.surface: Someone weighs whether cod is the better fish to choose in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod looks like the fish; it is Cape Cod in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a well-known headland, so Cod is an example of a cape.

clue.text: Longing to fill a large earthenware jug

indicators.note: the longing fills the next word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: per means a, as in once per day
an itch is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to pour something into a big clay jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a handle and lip, traditionally of earthenware.

clue.text: Rare beast in loch unexpectedly responsive to calming

indicators.note: something occurring unexpectedly does not follow the expected pattern, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
L is the abbreviation for loch on maps

explanation.surface: An unusual creature in a Scottish lake turns out to be surprisingly docile.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the Loch Ness monster; a loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be restrained can be held back or brought under control, hence calmed.

clue.text: Feature of Arctic upsetting Father Cecil endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the name loses its final letter
in a down clue, upsetting turns the pieces upside down so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the man's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Something in the Arctic is causing distress to a priest named Cecil.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar ice cap is the permanent sheet of ice covering the Arctic region.

clue.text: Sphere of activity involving students’ literary output?

blocks.note: uni is short for university, where students study
verse is poetry, a form of literary output

explanation.surface: A field of work involves the poems and essays students produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'students'' stands for their institution rather than the students themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's universe is their whole world or domain of experience and activity.

clue.text: Country fellow opening note

indicators.note: the fellow is opening the note, so he goes inside it and splits it apart

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
Al is a man's short name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A rustic man is tearing open a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country fellow' reads as a yokel, but 'Country' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: A sailor mostly caught one over in Corsican port

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word's last letter is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
Jack is a traditional name for a sailor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Roman numeral for one
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A seaman has too much to drink and is caught out in a Corsican harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught and over are cricket scoring abbreviations; an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajaccio is the capital and main port of Corsica, Napoleon's birthplace.

clue.text: Ruin pub importing crack cocaine yearly to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with signals only the starting letter of each of the two words before it
a thing importing something brings it inside, so the pub holds the next piece

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
to crack a problem is to solve it
first letters of cocaine and yearly

explanation.surface: A bar that smuggles in drugs every year is heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack cocaine' reads as one drug; crack is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvency is being unable to pay debts, which is financial ruin.

clue.text: Cake shop originally included in postman’s short run

indicators.note: originally points at how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept
the selected letter is placed inside the possessive word that follows
a word made short has been cut, here losing its final letter

blocks.note: Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman; this is his name with the possessive s
first letter of included
a run of matches or episodes is a series

explanation.surface: A baker's shop is among the stops on a mail carrier's abbreviated round.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character; the possessive s is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a French-style bakery selling pastries and gateaux.

clue.text: A large number in service

blocks.note: first meaning: a great quantity of things or people
second meaning: the Catholic eucharistic church service

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests many people at a service; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a great heap or crowd and the central act of Catholic worship.

clue.text: Made even, though impoverished, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, not seen, so its sound gives the answer

blocks.note: straitened circumstances are poor ones

explanation.surface: Someone has levelled things out despite being poor, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten is to make level or regular, removing bends or unevenness.

clue.text: Odd chap with a true claim to do with drugs

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the following letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A strange man makes a genuine assertion about narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to medicinal compounds, their manufacture or their sale.

clue.text: Plant in raid is past reforming

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: A police plant inside a gang is turning over a new leaf now the raid is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, popular in Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Sally’s type, extremely imaginative

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: a type is a sort or kind
the two outer letters of imaginative

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally has a wonderfully inventive personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name, but here it is a military sally, a sudden charge out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally and a sortie are both sudden attacks made by troops from a defended position.

clue.text: Key work going into beer and meat dish

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it, here inside the drink

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
ale is a kind of beer
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An important job involving beer and a plate of meat sounds like a pub kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, usually veal or pork, fried in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: A couple of cash handouts securing tropical tree

blocks.note: a divi is informal British for a dividend, a cash payout; a couple of them side by side

explanation.surface: Two cash payments are enough to buy a tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Divi-divi is a small tropical American tree whose curled pods are used for tanning.

clue.text: Like certain pressure one thus accepts round pub

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it in, so the following pieces go inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sic is Latin for thus, used in quotations
O is round in shape
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A drinker agrees to buy a round at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobaric describes conditions or lines on a weather map where atmospheric pressure is equal throughout.

clue.text: Porridge ingredient principally offered at breakfast, say

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: first letter of offered
taken as written
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Something served mainly at the morning meal goes into the porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, the main component of porridge.

clue.text: Mushroom I cooked initially with a fish

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as written
first letter of cooked

explanation.surface: Someone describes preparing mushrooms and fish for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' lets the a-plus-fish pair come first, ahead of the clue's opening pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is the name for gilled fungi such as the field mushroom and fly agaric.

clue.text: Again bury first of items stored by landlord?

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken
something stored by another is kept inside it

blocks.note: a renter can be one who rents property out, hence the question mark
first letter of items

explanation.surface: A tenant's belongings are being kept in storage by the property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: A renter usually pays rent; the question mark admits the less common sense of letting out.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinter is to place a body in a grave or tomb once more after exhumation.

clue.text: Outhouse quietly removed from scene of battle

indicators.note: removed from means one letter is taken out of the following word

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
Lepanto is where the 1571 naval battle against the Ottomans took place

explanation.surface: A shed has been discreetly taken away from an old battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or outbuilding whose roof rests against a larger building's wall.

clue.text: Popular archer one bloke’s primarily identified among eggheads

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the next two words are taken

blocks.note: something popular is in
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer
Roman numeral for one
a bloke is a gent, plus the possessive s
first letters of identified and among

explanation.surface: A well-liked bowman is spotted in a crowd of academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' looks like a link to the definition but its first letter is needed; bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is informal for highbrow thinkers, and the intelligentsia are a society's intellectual class.

clue.text: Group of girls needing drink, one Victor rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet; only one of the pair is removed

explanation.surface: Some young women need a drink after one man called Victor turned them down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a collective noun for a group, traditionally of girls or women.

clue.text: Arduous journey, ultimately not for the weak

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: final letters of not, for, the and weak

explanation.surface: A demanding expedition is described as only suitable for the strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, difficult walk or expedition, often over rough terrain.

clue.text: Bloomer made by tiny child inspiring key chamber work

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the child takes the next pieces inside

blocks.note: a mite is a tiny child
G is a musical key
a nonet is a piece of chamber music for nine players

explanation.surface: A small child makes a blunder that leads to a piece of chamber music.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer suggests a mistake, but it means something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant with small greenish flowers, so it is a bloomer.

clue.text: Gifted leader dismissed from board

indicators.note: dismissing the leader sends away the word's front letter

blocks.note: a board is a table

explanation.surface: A talented chairman has been sacked by the company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: Board looks like a company board, but here it is a plank or table top.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted and able are both adjectives meaning talented or skilled.

clue.text: Untidy woman’s hospital attendant

blocks.note: Di is a woman's name, plus the possessive s
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A hospital porter belonging to a particular woman is messy.
explanation.walkthrough: The orderly is tidy by name, yet the whole word means messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means lacking order or arrangement, so a cluttered room is untidy.
